Then

$ -\ln(1-x)+D=C+x+\dfrac{{{x}^{2}}}{2}+\dfrac{{{x}^{3}}}{3}+...+\dfrac{{{x}^{n}}}{n}+...$

We subtract $D$ from both sides, getting a new constant ($C-D$) on the right. Call that new constant $K$.

$ -\ln(1-x)=K+x+\dfrac{{{x}^{2}}}{2}+\dfrac{{{x}^{3}}}{3}+...+\dfrac{{{x}^{n}}}{n}+...$

Now let $x=0$ to see that $K=0$.

Hence

$ x+\dfrac{{{x}^{2}}}{2}+\dfrac{{{x}^{3}}}{3}+...+\dfrac{{{x}^{n}}}{n}+...= -\ln(1-x)$

question.content:
We know that

$\displaystyle\frac{1}{1-x}=1+x+{{x}^{2}}+{{x}^{3}}+...+{{x}^{n-1}}+...$

for $x\in\left(-1,1\right)$.

**Using this fact, find the function that corresponds to the following series.**

$\displaystyle x+\frac{{{x}^{2}}}{2}+\frac{{{x}^{3}}}{3}+...+\frac{{{x}^{n}}}{n}+...$ 

[[☃ radio 1]]
